newsitem.title: ESTONIA: TALLINNA OFF IN EARLY TRADE AMID MIXED MKT.
newsitem.headline: TALLINNA OFF IN EARLY TRADE AMID MIXED MKT.

text.p: Tallinna Pank was down slightly in early stock market trade on Friday after Tallinn city said it would sell its stake in the bank but dealers said the market was calm over the city's plans.
The rest of the market was mixed as the market shruged off a late slip in prices on Thursday, which was sparked by the announcement of the Tallinna Pank share sale.
"The news affected the mood of the market, but not Tallinna Pank so directly," one broker said.
But Tallinna Pank was slightly lower on a spread of 76.20/76.95 kroons versus Thurday's close of 77.00 although some dealers said the stock was still attractive.

"Tallinna Pank still remains one of the cheapest stocks on the market and the news of Tallinn city's sale was part of a generally known process of rationalising the city's investment portfolio," one analyst said.
"Some stocks fell slightly as the market opened, but the responses were mixed with buying pressure winning through," one dealer said.
Hanspank was higher on a bid/ask of 144.35/145.50 kroons against Thursday's close of 143.25 kroons. On Thursday the stock dipped by 4.50 kroons in trade just before closing.
"The market will be stable with no big falls expected and next week is not expected to be as volitile as this week as investors have not lost their optimism," he added.
"There is still a lot of good news about and so there is little reason for the market to be very negative," a dealer said.
